steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Reasons for fitness testing: Identify strengths and weaknesses - find out which components of fitness need improvement Monitor progress - compare test results over time to see if training is working Set baseline scores - establish starting points for setting targets and designing training programmes Compare against normative data - see how results compare to national averages for age and gender Provide motivation - give performers targets to aim for and a sense of achievement Assess suitability for a sport - determine if fitness levels meet the demands of a specific activity | Normative data: is a set of reference values (averages) that allow you to compare your test results against typical scores for your age and gender. Without normative data, a test score is just a number with no contex

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Which fitness test measures agility and briefly describe its protocol. | Name the test used to measure cardiovascular endurance and describe how it works. | Explain three reasons why fitness testing is carried out.

steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on Reasons for fitness testing, Normative data, Limitations, and one past-paper question.
